la:adj:anceps.html:
anceps (once ancipes, ; cf. Charis, pp. 67 and 96 P.; P.; with this form cf. procapis, Paul. ex Müll., and Corss. Ausspr. II. pp. 398, 591;
abl. sing. always ancipiti), cĭpĭtis, adj.
an-caput; cf. Paul. ex Müll.
.
Lit., that has two heads, twoheaded (cf.: biceps, praeceps, etc.; so only in the poets): Janus,; so (cf.: Janus bifrons,). —Hence also of a mountain which has two summits, two-peaked: acumen,.—
In gen.
Of an object whose qualities have significance in two respects, double, that extends on two opposite sides (while duplex is an object that exists in separate forms, twice. Thus anceps sententia is an opinion which wavers, fluctuates between two decisions, while duplex sententia is a twofold opinion): Post altrinsecus ancipes securiculast,the axe cuts on two sides, is two-edged,; so, ferrum, Lucil. ap. , and : securis,—Also, poet., of the contrast between great heat and cold: Ancipiti quoniam mucroni utrimque notantur, since things are marked by double point, i. e. one at one, another at the other end, : bestiae quasi ancipites in utrāque sede viventes,amphibious animals,; so in the histt. freq. of an attack, a contest, etc., on two different sides,: ita ancipiti proelio diu atque acriter pugnatum est, double, because contending with enemies both in front and in the rear, Herz.; so ; : periculum,: ancipitem pugnam hostibus facere, double, as given by horse and foot, : ancipiti metu et ab cive et ab hoste,twofold,; so, anceps terror,; : tumultus,: tela, shot or hurled from both sides, : ancipitia munimenta,on two sides,—
Trop., twofold: propter ancipitem faciendi dicendique sapientiam,: ancipites viae rationesque et pro omnibus et contra omnia disputandi,: adferre ancipitem curam cogitandi,a twofold care of thought,; so : jus anceps,the uncertainties of law,—
Wavering, doubtful, uncertain, unfixed, undecided (the prevalent signif. in Cic.): anceps fatorum via,: incertus exitus et anceps fortuna belli,: anceps proelii fortuna,: oraculum,: proelium,, and ; so esp. freq.: ancipiti Marte pugnare,to contend without deciding the contest,; : causa anceps,: genus causarum anceps, (cf.: genus causarum dubium, Auct. ad : dubium vel anceps,): fides,uncertain, wavering, fidelity,; so also, ancipites animi,.—Also ellipt.: Lucanus an Apulus, anceps, doubtful whether, etc., * .—
Dangerous, hazardous, perilous, critical (post-Aug.; esp. freq. in Tac.; never in Cic.): viae,: loca,: dubiā et interdum ancipiti fortunā,: anceps periculum,: ancipites morbi corporis,: cujus (Antonii) operā ex ancipiti morbo convaluerat,: Ideo et purgationibus (labruscum) ancipitem putant,: vox pro re publicā honesta, ipsi anceps,pernicious,: adulatio anceps si nulla et ubi nimia est,.—So subst., danger, hazard, peril, = periculum, discrimen: dubiā suorum re in anceps tractus vim legionum implorabat,: seu nihil militi seu omnia concederentur, in ancipiti res publica,: scelus inter ancipitia probatum,; 14, 22: facilius inter ancipitia clarescunt,: nova ambigua ancipitia malebat,: inter ancipitia deterrimum est media sequi,.!*? Comp., sup., and adv. not used.

la:noun:ancora.html:
ancŏra, ae (not anchŏra), f.
v. ango
, = ἄγκῦρα,
an anchor.
Lit.: Ancora fundabat naves,: jacere,to cast anchor,; so, mittere,to let go,: extendere,to put out,: naves deligare ad ancoras,: navem tenere in ancoris,: consistere ad ancoram,to lie at anchor,: naves in ancoris constiterunt, et saep.: solvere,to weigh anchor,; so, tollere,; so ; also, in gen.,to depart, go away,: vellere,: praecidere,to cut the cables,—
Trop., as a symbol of security, refuge, hope, support: ancora jam nostram non tenet ulla ratem,: ultima fessis ancora,; cf.: spem, quam sicut ancoram habemus,.—
Transf., an iron in the form of an anchor, .

la:noun:ancile.gloss: The sacred shield said to have fallen from heaven in the reign of Numa. It was the palladium of Rome.
senses: The sacred shield said to have fallen from heaven in the reign of Numa. It was the palladium of Rome.
la:noun:ancile.html:
ancīle (also ancŭle after ἀγκύλιον in Plut. Num.), is, n. (
gen. plur. ancilium, ; but anciliorum,; cf. P.) [prob. from ἀγκύλος, crooked, curved; v. ango],a small oval shield, Serv.; ; but specif. the shield that was said to have fallen from heaven in the reign of Numa

(hence, caelestia arma, ), and on the preservation of which the prosperity of Rome was declared to depend; whereupon Numa caused eleven others exactly like it to be made by the artist Mamurius Veturius. so that if the genuine one was lost, the fact could not be known. These shields were carefully preserved by the Salian priests in the temple of Mars, and every year in March carried about in solemn procession (ancilia movere), and then returned to their place (ancilia condere), ; ; ; ; ; ; v. Smith, Dict. Antiq.!*? Adj.: clipeis ancilibus,: arma ancilia,.

ancilla, ae, f.dim.
ancula
,

Trop.: terrā usus mortalium semper ancillā,.—As a term of reproach, of one servilely devoted to any thing: Fufidius ancilla turpis, Gerl.
